profileEvidence.summary: Quick in running and swimming in an 1814 account, the Saint John’s Water Dog was a working dog of Newfoundland’s fishermen. It retrieved fish that slipped off hooks near the surface and wildfowl taken while hunting, and helped haul winter fuel and timber. These native water dogs also supplied early stock for Britain’s Labrador Retriever.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A historical Newfoundland water dog, quick in water and used to retrieve loose fish and wildfowl and haul timber.
